claims.text: The equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni alloy and the compared equiatomic quaternary and ternary subsets are single-phase FCC after thermomechanical processing.
Differences in local lattice distortion cause differences in dislocation mobility across these alloys.
Multi-element interactions in the quinary alloy produce greater local lattice distortion than in the quaternary and ternary subsets.
Greater local lattice distortion in the quinary alloy lowers its stacking-fault energy.
Lower stacking-fault energy promotes planar dislocation slip.
Lower stacking-fault energy suppresses dislocation cross-slip.
Planar slip and suppressed cross-slip increase the work-hardening rate during deformation.
The proposed distortion-mediated dislocation behavior increases the strength of the quinary alloy relative to the quaternary and ternary alloys.
Under identical deformation conditions, the quinary alloy will have a higher yield strength than the quaternary and ternary subsets.
Under identical deformation conditions, the quinary alloy will have a higher work-hardening rate than the quaternary and ternary subsets.
The quaternary and ternary subsets will exhibit lower strengths than the quinary alloy.
The quaternary and ternary subsets may exhibit more cross-slip and different dislocation structures than the quinary alloy.
The proposed mechanism is restricted to room-temperature, quasi-static deformation of matched-grain-size, single-phase FCC alloys with identical thermomechanical histories.
Dynamic strain aging may also influence dislocation dynamics across these compositions.
